name: Sixteen steps · Ānāpānasati Sutta (MN 118)
summary: The Buddha’s sixteen steps of mindfulness of breathing, in four groups of four: the body (long, short, the whole body, calming the breath), feelings (rapture, pleasure, mental fabrication, calming it), the mind (sensing, gladdening, concentrating, releasing it) and mental qualities (inconstancy, dispassion, cessation, relinquishing), each held for a few breaths.

steps.text: Sit with legs crossed (or any steady seat), body erect, mindfulness to the fore. Mindful, breathe in; mindful, breathe out.
The body: discern a long breath as long and a short breath as short; breathe in and out sensitive to the entire body; calming bodily fabrication (the breath).
Feelings: breathe in and out sensitive to rapture, to pleasure, to mental fabrication (perceptions and feelings); calming mental fabrication.
The mind: sensitive to the mind, gladdening it, concentrating it, releasing it.
Mental qualities: focusing on inconstancy, dispassion (fading), cessation, relinquishing.

contraindications: No breath holds and no forcing: each step is noticed on the natural breath. If it becomes effortful, stay with the first tetrad (the beginner form).

facets.needs_teacher_note: A public teaching of the Buddha; a teacher helps with the later tetrads.

contraindications: No breath holds and no forcing

alternatives.when: for a more body-based way into the first tetrad

intro.caption: Sit with your legs crossed, or in any steady seat. Hold the body erect, and bring mindfulness to the fore.
Always mindful, breathe in. Mindful, breathe out.
When the breath is long, discern: I am breathing in long… I am breathing out long.

quote.text: Breathing in long, he discerns, ‘I am breathing in long’
quote.cite: The Buddha (Pali Canon), Ānāpānasati Sutta: Mindfulness of Breathing (MN 118), mn118:p18.s1 (tr. Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu)

intro.caption: When it is short, discern: I am breathing in short… breathing out short.
Breathe in sensitive to the entire body. Breathe out sensitive to the entire body.
Breathe in calming bodily fabrication, the breath itself. Breathe out, calming it.

quote.cite: The Buddha (Pali Canon), Ānāpānasati Sutta: Mindfulness of Breathing (MN 118), mn118:p45.s2 (tr. Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu)

intro.caption: Breathe in sensitive to rapture. Breathe out sensitive to rapture.
Breathe in sensitive to pleasure. Breathe out sensitive to pleasure.
Breathe in sensitive to mental fabrication: perceptions and feelings. Breathe out, sensitive to them.
Breathe in calming mental fabrication. Breathe out calming mental fabrication.
Breathe in sensitive to the mind. Breathe out sensitive to the mind.
Breathe in gladdening the mind. Breathe out gladdening the mind.
Breathe in concentrating the mind. Breathe out concentrating the mind.
Breathe in releasing the mind. Breathe out releasing the mind.
Breathe in focusing on inconstancy. Breathe out focusing on inconstancy.
Breathe in focusing on dispassion, on fading. Breathe out the same.
Breathe in focusing on cessation. Breathe out focusing on cessation.
Breathe in focusing on relinquishing. Breathe out focusing on relinquishing.

sources.cite: Ānāpānasati Sutta (MN 118), tr. Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu, dhammatalks.org (also Handful of Leaves vol. 2, rev. 2017)

level.note: the first tetrad suits anyone; the full sixteen ask for a settled mind (beginner form = first tetrad)

meta.confidence_note: Built by the text-to-practice pipeline from MN 118 (the sixteen steps, p17–p21; notes 1–4 read for “to the fore”, the entire body and the two fabrications). The sutta sets no length per step: each step gets three breaths (rule step-breaths); extra session time is open sitting at the end, never extra steps. The establishings of mindfulness and factors for awakening are left to the Theory tab.
